Resettlement of Tribals of Jaduguda 
*642. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT RAO: Will the PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Jharkhandis have approached him for resettlement of 
tribals of Jaduguda, away from the Uranium mining affected area in 
Jharkhand; 
(b) if so, what are their apprehensions in respect of radio -active 
material exposure in that area; and 
(c) the action proposed to rehabilitate them? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC 
ENERGY (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) to (c) An organisation 
titled the "Jharkhandis Organisation Against Radiation" (JOAR) has recently 
submitted a representation to Prime Minister making a number of demands 
in the context of (alleged) adverse impact of the operations of the Uranium 
Corporation of India Ltd. (UCIL), a Central public sector undertaking of the 
Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), at Jaduguda in the East Singhbhum 
District of Bihar. Apart from alleging about the impact of the uranium 
mining operations (low -level radiation) on the environment, health, safety 
and socio -economy of Jaduguda area, demands have also been made on 
issues like constitution of a multi -disciplinary team from the All India 
Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi to study the above mentioned 
(alleged) impact, evacuation of villages around the exist ing tailing 
ponds/dams of UCIL to safer places and their resettlement, establishment of 
a medical centre in or around Jaduguda to treat low -level radiation related 
diseases, stoppage of (alleged) "import" of radio active waste and radio -
medical waste into Jaduguda for (alleged) dumping storage and autonomy of 
the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) 
UCIL operates three uranium mines at Jaduguda, Bhatin and 
Narwapahar respectively and a uranium -processing mill at Jaduguda. Since 
UCIL's inception, the radiat ion levels in and around its mines and plants 
have been continuously monitored by the Health Physics Unit of the Bhabha 
Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of the DAE. The Health 
Physics Unit stationed at Jaduguda consists of qualified specia lists in the 
relevant field. 
The radiation levels in and around Jaduguda on account of releases 
from the mines/plants of UCIL are well within the limits prescribed in this 
behalf by the AERB which are, in turn, based on the recommendations of the 
International Commission on Radiological Protection. 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [11 May, 2000] 
Surveys conducted in the recent past by teams of medical doctors and 
other specialists, including doctors from the Tata Main.Hospital, Jamshedpur 
and Health Department of the Governm ent of Bihar and health physicists and 
medical officers from BARC, have also established that the specific cases of 
diseases examined by the teams have no relation to radiation. Recent 
radiation survey of the area around Jaduguda has also reconfirmed that the 
operations of UCIL have not resulted in any increase in the background 
radiation levels beyond those prescribed by the AERB. 
About 51 acres of private land were acquired by UCIL in the recent 
past, through the local District administration, for constru ction of its third 
stage tailing pond. Full compensation for the land so acquired has been paid 
by UCIL. Alternate land has also been provided by the District administration 
for housing of the families whose lands/houses were acquired. This land has 
been l evelled by UCIL which has also provided drinking water tube wells 
there. Additional financial assistance (over and above due compensation for 
acquisition) has also been committed by UCIL to each affected family for 
construction of dwelling houses. Finally,  51 persons from 46 families whose 
land and houses were acquired and 10 persons from 10 families from which 
only lands were acquired have been provided employment in UCIL. Thus, all 
necessary steps have been taken by UCIL, in consultation with the local 
District administration, for resettlement of the families whose lands/houses 
were acquired for construction of the third stage tailing pond. 
In view of the fact that the operations of the UCIL have not led to any 
radiation related diseases in the area around  Jaduguda, the question of setting 
up a medical centre in or around Jaduguda for treatment of such (alleged) 
diseases does not arise. 
Magnesium-di-uranate (MDU) produced by UCIL is sent in safe 
containers to the Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC), Hyderabad for fabrication of 
fuel for the nuclear power reactors. The raffinate generated after extraction of 
uranium at the NFC is brought back to UCIL for further reprocessing in the 
uranium mill at Jaduguda and recovery of the residual uranium value 
therefrom. No radioactive or radiochemical waste is being dumped by UCIL, 
as alleged by JOAR. The effuent from the tailing ponds is treated to the 
prescribed standards at the effluent treatment plant of UCIL and the treated 
water is mostly reused in the uranium mill. Only a small quantity of the 
treated water, meeting the prescribed norms, is discharged in a stream. 

[11 May,  2000] RAJYA SABHA 
The AERB has been established under the provisions of the Atomic 
Energy Act, 1962 and has the necessary functional autonomy to discha rge 
the duties and responsibilities entrusted to it, including those in the area of 
radiological safety. 
Supply of Desulphurised Petrol 
*643. SHRI SANTOSH. BAGRODIA: Will the Minister of 
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government hav e plan to ensure supply of unadulterated 
petrol and diesel at retail outlets; 
(b) whether Government plan to supply ultra low sulphur diesel with 
sulphur content of 0.05% (maximum) all over the country; and 
(c) if so, the details there if? 
THE MINISTER OF PET ROLE UM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI 
RAM NAIK): (a) The oil marketing companies supply petrol and diesel as 
per specifications laid down by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) all over the 
country. In order to ensure that the quality of petrol and diesel is maintained 
as per BIS specifications, oil marketing companies carry out regular/surprise 
checks of retail outlets,'to control various malpractices including 
adulteration. In addition, special drives are lauached by the oil companies 
both on their own and also under dir ection of Government from time to time 
to check malpractices. 
Further to check adulteration Government have decided to promulgate 
Solvent, Slop, Raffinate {Acquisition, Sale, Storage and Prevention of Use in 
Automobile) Order, and Naphtha (Acquisition, Sale, Storage and Prevention 
of Use in Automobile) Order. 
(b) and (c) Oil marketing companies have already introduced ultra low 
sulphur petrol for all categories of vehicles in the National Capital Region 
since 1.4.2000. 
Oil Industry has also introduced ultra  low sulpur diesel with 0.05% 
maximum sulphur content for new non - commercial vehicles through select 
outlets in the National Capital Region since 1.4.2000. 
In order to supply 0.05% maximum sulphur content diesel all over the 
country, modifications in the existing refineries need to be carried out. An

Projects behind Schedule 
*644. SHRI NARENDRA MOHAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that about 430 projects are behind schedule and 
this has adversely affected the approved cost of these projects and 
consequently there has been substantial increase in the costs; 
(b) what measures are being adopted to contain time and cost overrun; 
and 
(c) whether there is any system of annual or mid -term appraisal of 
such projects and whether the machinery to cond uct this appraisal is 
adequate or alert? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE OF 
THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) Out of 452 
projects presently on the monitor of the Ministry of Statistics & Programme 
Implementation, 204 projects are having cost overrun and 205 projects are 
having time overrun. With respect to the original approved cost, cost overrun 
of all the 452 projects is 36%. 
(b) The measures taken to reduce time and cost overruns of these 
projects include the following:— 
(i) Review of projects on monthly as well as quarterly b asis by the 
Government. This enables the Government to identify the 
constraints and help them to remove these constraints and to resolve 
the problems affecting the implementation of the projects; 
(ii) Indepth critical review of the progress by the Project Authorities and 
Administrative Ministries and follow up with the State 
Governments

(for acquisition of land and provision of infrastructure facilities like 
water and power, ensuring law and order at project site, etc.). with 
manufacturers for expediting supply of equipment, with contractors, 
consultants and other concerned agencies to minimise delays; 
(iii)  Setting up of an Empowered Committee in each administrative 
Ministry for resolution of problem; 
(iv) Bringing modificati ons in the Land Acquisition Act and

(v) Appointment of a nodal officer for each project co -terminus with the

(c) All major projects costing Rs. 100 crores and above are intensively 
reviewed every month. Besides, all projects are also monitored on a 
quarterly basis and specific corrective measures are suggested to the 
concerned administrative Ministries to avoid further delays and cost 
overruns. Quarterly Annual Performance Review Meetings and Empowered 
Committee Meetings for mid term appraisal of projects are held by the 
concerned Administrative Ministries for review o f status. Standing 
Committees have been set up in 22 administrative Ministries to go into the 
causes of time and cost overruns for projects costing Rs. 50 crores and above 
and to initiate corrective measures. The Reports of these Committees fora 
part of the notes for revised cost estimates of the projects with time and cost 
overruns and are submitted to the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.

Fresh Diplomatic Initiatives with Gulf Countries 
*645. SHRI SWARAJ KAUSHAL: Will t he Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any proposal to initiate fresh diplomatic 
relationship with Muslim countries in the Gulf region after having close 
relationship with America; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether he has visited the Muslim countries of Gulf region in this 
regard;'and 
(d) if so, the outcome thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT 
SINGH): (a) and (b) The Gulf region is India's neighbourhood. India enjoys 
traditionally close, historical and multidi mensional ties with the Gulf 
countries. These relations are neither -dependent nor subject to India's 
relations with other countries. 
(c) and (d) Ministerial level consultations continue to be held regularly 
on an ongoing basis to further strengthen and enh ance our political, 
economic, and cultural relations with the countries of the Gulf. It is in this 
context that visits to and from the Gulf countries have taken place. All these 
visits have contributed to further enhancing India's profile in the region and  
improving relations bilaterally. 
Corruption in project Clearance 
*646. SHRI RAM DEO BHANDARY: Will the PRIME MINISTER 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that corruption is the first major problem as the 
funds earmarked for a particular project are not reaching their intended 
beneficiaries; 
(b) whether the above observations made by Piara Singh Khabra as 
reported in Times of India dated 7th April, 2000, are true; and 
(c) what steps are being taken to clean the administration at all levels? 
THE MINISTER OF ST ATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME

IMPLEMENTATION AND THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE 
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES IN  THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) and (b) 
Shri Piara Singh Khabra (of the Indian origin), a Member of the House of 
Commons, UK, during his interview with Mr. Gurmukh Singh (The Times of 
India) has observed: 
"As we see it, corruption is the first major problem..It is hampering 
India's progress as the funds earmarked for a particular project are not 
reaching the intended beneficiaries." 
(The Times of India, Delhi edition — 6th April, 2000.) 
The statement does not seem to pertain to Central Sector projects per 
se, but to the plans and programmes undertaken by the Government in 
general. Analysis carried out by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation in respect of projects on its monitor indicates that the 
following are the major factors accounting for time and cost over-runs: 
(i) Fund constraints 
(ii) Land acquisition problems 
(iii) Delay in civil works 
(iv) Delay in award of contracts 
(v) Delay in procurement and receipt of equipment.    
Apart fro m projects, evaluations are conducted periodically to gauge 
the efficacy of the Programmes in removing poverty. The Ministry of Rural 
Development carries out concurrent evaluation of anti -poverty programmes 
implemented in rural areas. The results of the fi fth round of concurrent 
evaluation of Integrated Rural Development Programme (1995 -96) indicate 
that though a large number of beneficiaries have substantially improved their 
living conditions, major areas of concern remain. Scheduled Castes and 
Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries were only 40 per cent of the total beneficiaries 
assisted as against the target of 50 per cent. Only 14 per cent women -headed 
households received assistance. Around 22 per cent of the old IRDP 
beneficiaries had reportedly made payments t o Government/bank staff for 
getting IRDP assistance. Some of the other evaluation studies commissioned 
by the Ministry of Rural Development and the Planning

Commission have also indicated that assistance i n some cases was provided 
to families which were not below poverty line. The evaluation of Wage 
Employment Programme shows that these programmes were better targeted 
and did provide employment opportunities in lean season. Even in such 
programmes work was executed often through contractors which was not 
permitted and muster rolls were not properly maintained. 
(c) As for steps to combat corruption, the Government has recently 
taken the following initiatives:— 
(i) The Central Vigilance Commission has been vested powers vide para 
3(v) of Department of Personnel & Training Resolution No. 
371/20/99-AVD.III dated 4th April, 1999 to exercise 
superintendence over the vigilance administration. The Commission 
has issued several instructions to reduce the scope of corr uption, 
such as, creating a culture of honesty, greater transparency in 
administration, electronics clearance system and computerization of 
banks, sensitizing the public etc. The Central Vigilance 
Commission has also issued Special Chapters on vigilance 
management in public sector banks and public sector undertakings. 
(ii) The Central Vigilance Commission Bill has been introduced in the 
Lok Sabha on 20.12.1999 to confer statutory status upon the Central 
Vigilance Commission and to incorporate the other dire ctions of the 
Supreme Court in Vineet Narain vs Union of India. The Bill stands 
referred to the Joint Committee of both the Houses of Parliament on 
21.12.1999 for consideration. 
(iii) Some of the major steps taken to insulate the CBI from extraneous 
influences and to improve its functioning are: 
• Director, CBI has been given a minimum tenure of 2 years. 
• A CBI Selection Board has been constituted to make 
recommendations for the appointment of Director, CBI and for 
reduction/extension in tenure/pre -mature repatriation of officers of 
the rank of SP and above in CBI. 
• 183 posts, including technical posts, have been sanctioned for 
augmenting the Special Crime Division and Economic Offences 
Wing of the CBI.

(iv)  Lok Pal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 3.8.1998 to set up 
the Lok Pal to look into the allegations of corruption against high 
public functionaries. The Bill, however, lapsed on the dissolution of

into self -help groups, their capacity building, planning of activity 
cluster, infrastructure build -up, technology, credit and marketing 
facilities. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana has been restructured with the

provide employment in lean season. Self -employment and Wage -
employment Schemes in urban areas were also restructured w.e.f. 
1.12.1997 under Swaranjayanti Shahri Rozgar yojana. The 
Government has taken measures to ensure active participation of the 
people as partners in the process of development.
